scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Buzzard Lope originated within enslaved African American communities in the Southern United States, likely developing as an adaptation of a similar West African dance tradition.
It was first documented in Georgia during the 1880s.
Following its rural origins, the dance crossed into theatrical entertainment and became widely popular within the Minstrel Show repertoire alongside dances like the cakewalk and juba dance.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance enacts a dramatic representation of a turkey buzzard circling and preparing to feed upon a carcass, historically reported as either a dead mule or cow.
It combines precise animal mimicry with a distinct comedic sensibility known as hokum.
Today it is a historical tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers stretch out their arms to mimic birds of prey while executing a shuffle step and a small hop around the dance space.
In the center of the floor, a piece of cloth is laid down to represent carrion.
While the dancer circles this focal object, people gathered on the sidelines clap their hands and pat their thighs to generate the rhythm.
Watch for Buzzard Wing Hop.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The dance is rooted in the Southern States and was specifically noted in Georgia; regional variations are reflected in whether the central carrion is characterized as a dead mule or a dead cow.
The Buzzard Lope shares theatrical lineage with the cakewalk and the juba dance, emerging from enslaved African American traditions adapted from West African antecedents.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Place a piece of cloth on the ground to establish the central point.
Step 2: Extend both arms fully outward to imitate the outstretched wings of a buzzard.
Footwork from the sources: A shuffle step combined with a small hop executed along a circular pathway.

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Execute a low shuffle step moving along a circular path around the cloth.
Step 4: Add a small hop into the shuffle while maintaining the arm extension and circular trajectory.
Drill: Extend arms horizontally, holding posture steady for two full revolutions.

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.

Drill: Add gentle wing-like arm tilts while walking the perimeter.
